# A card held by a drag stays rendered when its long column's window moves

## Context

Profiling #21627 (a board of 10,000 cards; New holds 6,200) at `dev` `f6afbf6be3`, headless Chromium, 1440 × 900. A card in the middle of New drags into Triage at scroll offsets 0, 3,000 and 60,000 px, and both headers change. The last card, with New scrolled to its end, does not: the drag never enters Triage, the drop commits nothing, and the drag proxy stays on screen after the release. #21627's AC requires exactly that drag ("A card from the end of the longest column can be dragged into another column"), so this leaf blocks it.

## The Problem

Read in the App Worker mid-drag: `zone.isEnteringColumn` stays `true` and `activeColumn` stays New. The held card `t-6200` is no longer in New's body (`parentId: null`, unmounted). New's window moved back to start at 6081, so its last rendered card is `t-6191`. Moving the held card up the column shifted the body's scroll offset, `applyBodyScroll` slid the window, and the reprojection dropped the held card from the component tree.

`enterColumn` then awaits `card.promiseUpdate()` on a card that will never update. `trap()` rejects only on destroy, so the entry never settles. Every later move queues as pending, and `processDragEnd` waits on `columnEntry` forever.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Column#selectWindow` (`src/board/Column.mjs:228-237`) clamps `windowStart` to the records and slices `windowCapacity` (`maxRenderedCards` + `overscan`) of them. `Column#applyBodyScroll` (`:283-287`) moves the window on scroll through `setWindowStart` → `board.reconcileColumn`.
- During a drag the held card stays a component of its source column's body, and only DOM nodes move (`src/board/SortZone.mjs` class JSDoc: "During the drag only DOM deltas move"). The zone holds `dragComponent` and `dragRecord` until the gesture ends.
- `SortZone#enterColumn` awaits `card.promiseUpdate()` through `trap()` (`src/core/Base.mjs:1271`), which settles only on resolve or destroy.
- Design authority: n/a. It is a hang with a stuck proxy, a defect by any reading: the class JSDoc states that a drop commits or a cancel writes nothing, and here neither happens.

## The Fix

While the board's sort zone holds a card, a sliced column's `selectWindow` keeps that record inside its window, moving the window as little as it must. The scroll offset realigns on the next scroll after the drop.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A unit arm reproduces the eviction: in a sliced column with its window at the end, a drag holds the last card and the window then moves back. The held card stays in the column's body, and the window moves only as far as it must. It fails on `dev`. The entry and the drop are shown in a real browser: the unit environment's mocked update cycle cannot settle an entry after a reprojection.
- [ ] #21627's example drags the last card of its longest column into another column (that PR's e2e spec).
- [ ] The board unit family and `test/playwright/e2e/board/` stay green.

## Out of Scope

The example (#21627). Changing `trap()` to time out. Window sizing.

## Avoided Traps

- **Freezing every window during a drag.** The other columns keep scrolling, and so does the source column, as long as the held card stays inside.
